summary: Redrew the boundary lines of the Medicine Bow Forest Reserve in Wyoming, set out the new limits, and fixed a date when lands left outside the reserve would open to settlement.

Changed passport rules so U.S. diplomats and consuls could issue passports to residents of the nation's insular possessions who swore allegiance to the United States and backed their application with two credible witnesses.

Laid out the rules for getting a U.S. passport at home: only the Secretary of State issues them, applicants must owe allegiance to the United States, and applications take the form of a sworn affidavit with a personal description.

Set the rules for issuing passports in the insular possessions, directing applicants to the chief executive of each possession and requiring a sworn affidavit from anyone owing allegiance to the United States.
Amended Civil Service Rule VI so one confidential clerk to the commissioner of immigration at the port of New York could be hired without examination.
Amended Civil Service Rule VI to exempt one immigrant inspector and law clerk in the New York immigration commissioner's office from examination.
Created the Mount Graham Forest Reserve in Arizona Territory, describing its boundaries and closing the land to settlement.
Reserved Miraflores Island in San Juan Harbor, Puerto Rico, as a site for a quarantine station or marine hospital run by the Public Health and Marine Hospital Service.
Made Ellen W. Fitzsimmons eligible to move from the abolished office of Commissioner of Railroads to the Post Office Department, waiving a civil-service transfer rule.
Ordered compulsory retirement for Revenue Cutter Service officers once they reached age sixty-four.
Established the Lincoln Forest Reserve in New Mexico Territory, setting its boundaries and reserving the land from settlement.
Set apart the Chiricahua Forest Reserve in Arizona Territory, describing its limits and closing the land to settlement.
Allowed a $1,000-a-year War Department clerk, to be detailed for duty at the White House, to be appointed without civil-service examination.
Gave seamen gunners, and enlisted men holding certificates from the seaman gunner class of the petty officers' schools, two dollars a month in extra pay.
Amended Civil Service Rule VI so the collector at the port of New York could have one solicitor appointed without examination.
Proclaimed that the supplemental agreement between the United States and the Muskogee (Creek) Nation, approved by Congress and by the Creek national council, was ratified and had the force of law.
Reserved described lands in Nebraska for the Department of Agriculture to use for experimental tree planting.
Made John T. Heck eligible for reinstatement in the Government Printing Office no matter how long he had been out of the service.
Set regulations governing the discharge of enlisted men from the Navy.
Created the Little Belt Mountains Forest Reserve in Montana, defining its boundaries and reserving the land from settlement.
Established the Madison Forest Reserve in Montana, laying out its boundaries and closing the land to settlement.

Widened a civil-service exception so Marine-Hospital Service workers hired temporarily to keep contagious diseases from entering or spreading, in the United States or elsewhere, needed no examination.

Reserved Chichagof, Kupreanof, Kuiu, Zarembo and Prince of Wales islands and neighboring islands in Alaska as the Alexander Archipelago Forest Reserve, while protecting valid rights held under the 1867 treaty with Russia.
Returned 40 acres once held for the Fort Sill Indian sub-agency to the public domain so the nearby city of Lawton, Oklahoma Territory, could acquire it for a cemetery.
Established the Absaroka Forest Reserve in Montana, describing its boundaries and reserving the land from settlement.
Directed the Civil Service Commission to reissue a 1901 certificate naming Raplie M. Cheshire, who had declined the appointment by mistake.
Allowed David Lynch to be appointed cable engineer for the Signal Service in Manila without civil-service examination.
Established the Nambe Pueblo Indian Reservation in New Mexico Territory for the use and occupation of the Nambe Pueblo Indians, subject to valid existing rights.
Closed the executive departments, the Government Printing Office and the Washington navy yard so federal workers could join or honor the Grand Army of the Republic parade of October 8, 1902.
Let workers on the Government Printing Office building be kept on, without regard to civil-service rules, for work on the War College and Washington Barracks.
Struck section 6 of Civil Service Rule VIII, changing the rules on apportionment of appointments.

Directed that the rules against soliciting political contributions from federal officers and employees be reaffirmed and enforced, after an Attorney General's opinion on circulars sent by party committees in Pennsylvania and Ohio.
Named Thursday, November 27, 1902, a national day of thanksgiving.
Amended paragraph 660 of the Consular Regulations of 1896 so that gold or silver bullion was not treated as money or currency.
Established the Malaga Military Reservation in Samar Island Province, Philippine Islands.
Enlarged the Fort William H. Seward Military Reservation at Haines, Alaska, to take in a clay deposit for road-making, and reserved the east shore of Chilkat Inlet near Dyea for military use.

places.name: Fort William H. Seward Military Reservation

summary: Added described lands to the Greenville Indian Industrial Training School Reservation in California.

places.name: Greenville Indian Industrial Training School Reservation

summary: Established the Olongapo Naval Station in Zambales Province on Luzon, Philippine Islands.
Defined the duties of the Secretary to the President.
Shrank the White Mountain or San Carlos Indian Reservation in Arizona Territory, returning described lands to the public domain.

places.name: White Mountain or San Carlos Indian Reservation

summary: Authorized F. L. Templeton's appointment as a clerk in the Post Office Department without regard to civil-service rules.
Allowed Charles W. Newton to be appointed physician at the Western Navajo Agency without examination.
Authorized reinstating Stainslaus M. Hamilton as a clerk in the Department of State without regard to civil-service rules.
Extended the temporary appointments of eight Internal Revenue Service clerks for sixty days.
Set apart public lands in the Luquillo area of Puerto Rico as the Luquillo Forest Reserve, defining its limits by latitude and longitude and reserving it from settlement.
Amended the civil-service rules to require that laborers doing the work of classified employees be certified through the Civil Service Commission.
Placed the Midway Islands under the jurisdiction and control of the Navy Department.
Amended the civil-service rules to bar certain transfers when a position could be filled by promotion.

Merged the Yellowstone, Teton and Absaroka forest reserves, with added lands, into a single Yellowstone Forest Reserve spanning Wyoming and Montana, superseding earlier proclamations and protecting existing rights.
Allowed F. A. Collins to be appointed private secretary to the Public Printer without examination.
Authorized reinstating Oscar Wenderoth as senior draftsman in the Treasury Department without regard to civil-service rules.

Opened to disposal the former Cheyenne River Agency tract on Sioux lands along the Missouri River, since the agency and school buildings had moved, except 160 acres held by the St. Johns Mission School.
Permitted temporary clerks at naval stations in the insular possessions to receive permanent appointments.
Removed the civil-service rule provision that had let aliens qualify for the position of copperplate map engraver.
Called the U.S. Senate into extraordinary session at the Capitol at noon on March 5, 1903.
Authorized appointing a translator in the Bureau of Insular Affairs without examination.

Moved the State Department's Revolutionary archives, including the Continental Congress records and the papers of Washington, Madison, Jefferson, Hamilton, Monroe and Franklin, to the Library of Congress for preservation and public use.
Authorized Horatio C. Pollock's appointment as a clerk at military headquarters in the Philippine Islands without examination.
Established the Valdez Signal Station on the east shore of Valdez Bay, Alaska, for the Signal Corps' Fort Liscum–Fort Egbert military telegraph line.
Allowed William J. Lee to be appointed telegrapher in the Department of Commerce and Labor without examination.
Set aside Pelican Island in Florida's Indian River as a preserve and breeding ground for native birds, with its boundaries described.
Issued a new set of civil-service rules replacing those of May 6, 1896, barring political or religious tests and coercion and requiring examinations for the classified service.
Directed the Civil Service Commission to help departments set up competitive registration of laborers and workmen in offices outside Washington, starting in large cities.
Authorized James A. Dumont's appointment as inspector of hulls in the Steamboat Inspection Service without regard to civil-service rules.
Moved the St. Cloud, Minnesota, land office to Cass Lake and shifted described lands among the St. Cloud, Marshall, Crookston and Duluth land districts.
Ordered the Marshall, Minnesota, land office moved to St. Cloud, effective July 1, 1903.
Authorized Exum L. Holland's transfer to inspector in the Customs Service without regard to civil-service rules.
Clarified that the civil-service rules of March 20, 1903, did not give permanent appointments to employees serving under sections 13-16 of Rule VIII of the 1896 rules.
Required the executive departments to furnish the Secretary of the Interior with information for preparing the Official Register.
Allowed Albert U. Wyman to be appointed clerk in the Office of the Treasurer without examination.
Authorized a permanent appointment for Lucas Blanco as messenger in the Customs Service without examination.
Established the Skagway Military Reservation, 466.12 acres at Skagway, Alaska.
Created the Manti Forest Reserve in Utah, setting out its boundaries and reserving the land from settlement.
Established the Logan Forest Reserve in Utah, describing its limits and closing the land to settlement.
Established the Torrey Barracks Military Reservation at Malabang on Mindanao, Philippine Islands, and defined its boundaries.
Transferred described lands from the St. Cloud, Minnesota, land district to the Duluth land district, effective June 30, 1903.
Amended paragraph 463 of the Consular Regulations of 1896 on the issuing of circulars.

Combined the Lewis and Clarke and Flathead forest reserves in Montana into one Lewis and Clarke Forest Reserve with new boundaries, adding some lands, dropping others, and setting a date for excluded lands to open.
Reserved the Isabela de Basilan Reservation at Zamboanga, the Poloc Reservation at Parang and Fort San Pedro at Cebu, Philippine Islands, for naval purposes.
Reserved described public lands in Puerto Rico for naval purposes under the 1902 act letting the President keep federal lands on the island for public uses.
Reserved property at Ponce, Mayaguez and San Juan, Puerto Rico, for the use of the federal courts, district attorney and marshal.
Kept described federal lands in Puerto Rico for public uses, including a public building site in San Juan, a marine hospital, custom-houses and lighthouses.
Reserved lands in Puerto Rico for naval purposes and allowed the Secretary of the Navy and the Governor of Puerto Rico to submit memoranda of understanding on how the lands would be used.
Withdrew The Presidio, the penitentiary grounds and buildings at San Juan, from the June 26, 1903, proclamation reserving Puerto Rico lands for naval use.
Established a group of military reservations across Puerto Rico, including Aibonito, Aguadilla, Fajardo, Henry Barracks at Cayey, Mayagüez, San Juan and sites around San Juan Harbor.
Authorized reinstating Charles B. Terry as a clerk in the Post Office Department after he had been shifted off the temporary roll and missed classification.
Dropped the age requirement from unskilled-labor tests for Civil War soldiers and sailors, judging them instead on physical fitness, character, industry and adaptability for manual labor.
Established the Nonucan Military Reservation, later Camp Overton, on Mindanao, Philippine Islands.
Approved appointing ten people to positions in the Department of Commerce and Labor without civil-service examination, citing each one's special qualifications.
Waived the one-year reinstatement limit so Sarah McLanahan, widowed with three children, could return as a sewer at the Government Printing Office.
Granted Navy gun captains on regular detail five dollars a month in extra pay.
Approved Civil Service Commission extensions of temporary job employments beyond six months, covering carpenters, clerks and other workers at posts from Monterey to Fort Niagara.
Let Annie M. West and Sadie B. Yates be reinstated as sewer and telephone operator at the Government Printing Office despite the one-year reinstatement limit.
Allowed Luther M. Walter to be appointed law clerk in the Interstate Commerce Commission after a noncompetitive examination.
Established the Camp Hartshorne Military Reservation at Laguan, Samar Island, Philippine Islands.
